The rider's consent is real and pre-segment: the driver asked at 12:26 whether he could "go round via Sims Avenue" because PIE traffic was building up [F8], and the rider herself replied at 12:27 "Sure, go ahead." [F9], before the segment's 12:29 start [F3]; the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F10]. That is a rider message sent before the segment, so RD-5 is engaged. The driver's ask named Sims Avenue ('ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?', F8) and the rider's 'Sure, go ahead.' (F9) is an agreement to that named road, not a general route licence, so consent covers driving on Sims Avenue only.

The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so the unexempted detour's extra kilometres entered the metered fare and must be refunded per kilometre; the fare facts fix the per-km rate at $1.4098/km (F4, distance fare $27.35 ÷ 19.40 km, F7).

The waiting fee of $0.11 (F5) is 0.4 metered waiting minutes during a stop inside the detour segment; since the segment itself is unexempted, its waiting time follows the segment and should also be returned, giving a total of $4.72.

The driver already has 2 upheld disputes in 90 days (F17), but since route disputes among them are 0 (F17), RD-6's repeated-route-offence condition is not met and no account flag is requested on this record.
The complaint contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F8, F9, F11), so no escalation under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 is warranted.

The driver's contemporaneous reason is corroborated by a real congestion record — PIE speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 12:04–12:29 (F12) covering the moment just before the turn — which supports his 'reasonable cause' story under RD-4(b) even though F14 shows no incident.

The rider's agreement is a named-road authorisation to drive via Sims Avenue, and the only record tying the driven segment to a road is F3, which gives the segment's time and distance but no road name, and the chat record F10 shows no further message placing the car on Sims Avenue; no record places the segment anywhere else either, so on the correspondence question the segment is undetermined rather than shown to be a detour off the agreed road (F3, F10).

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, any non-exempt segment distance flows into the fare: the fare shows 3.93 km billed as excess distance at $1.4098/km = $5.54 (F4) within a total of $41.09 (F7), so the maximum exposure in issue on this segment is at most that distance-fare element, computed from F4.
The waiting item billed is a metered waiting unit of only 0.4 min = $0.11 (F5), which on a metered trip is chargeable waiting time and is not part of any route refund (F5, F4).

No safety escalation arises from this record: the chat contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F8, F9, F10, F11), and there is no accident or injury fact in the case.

The $0.11 waiting unit (F5) was recorded during the unexempted detour window (F3), so on a segment the rider never agreed to it is not exempt from return; if the judge declines to follow the segment, we accept the $0.11 alone.
Agreed: nothing in the chat or the driver's statement reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F8, F9, F10, F11), so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation.

The rider's own brief is right that no fact names the road of the detour, and I do not claim named_road_tied; but the absence of a road name means the tie between the agreed road and the driven segment is unproven, which is RD-5's undetermined situation (G13), not proof that the driver drove somewhere else — no fact (F3, F8, F9, F10) places the car off Sims Avenue, so the segment cannot be converted into a driver_errand.

Agreed that F14 defeats RD-4(a); the PIE band 2 for 12:04–12:29 (F12) is offered only as RD-4(b) corroboration, which on the MVP default does not exempt the segment on its own — the driver's exemption stands on the rider's own words in F9 under RD-5, not on RD-4.

The arithmetic of $4.61 (3.27 km × $1.4098/km, F3 and F4) is not disputed, but it is only payable if the segment is unexempted; F3's own figure shows the segment distance is part of the metered route actually agreed in F9, and RD-2's '未豁免段以外的里程差额不退' likewise bars the $0.93 difference, so no partial refund is owed on this record.
